title: Microscopy-based cellular contractility assay for adult, neonatal, and hiPSC cardiomyocytes
protocol: Adjust microscope settings for different cell types as necessary.
Increase contrast by adjusting diaphragm aperture, focus, and light intensity.
Use mature sarcomere structure for robust contrast in adult cardiomyocytes.
Decrease contrast settings for neonatal-CMs and hiPSC-CMs due to lower intrinsic contrast.
Account for weaker contraction in neonatal-CMs and hiPSC-CMs compared to adult-CMs.
Adjust for spontaneous syncytium self-organization in neonatal-CMs and hiPSC-CMs.
Adjust the focus until the cell border is delimited with minimum edge brightness.
Make small adjustments using the fine focus control to ensure the cell border is sharp and without any optical bloom.
Set up the diaphragm to achieve sufficient contrast without making the image overly dark or lacking in detail.
Adjust lighting and camera settings so that the mean gray value histogram is centered on the half-maximal range (127 for an 8-bit image).
Ensure there are no pixel intensities close to zero or saturation in the gray value histogram.
Start with the microscope setup for Kohler illumination.
Open the diaphragm fully, resulting in low contrast and little cell border delineation.
Slowly close the diaphragm until the delineation of the cell edge and nucleus appears and contrast is optimized.
Set up the camera for image collection.
Select the image window size to record just the area of interest around the cell.
For adult-CMs experiments, use an image window size of 640 horizontal ×200 vertical pixels.
For neonatal-CM or hiPSC-CM, use an image window size of 640 × 480 pixels.
If more than 5% of the adult-CMs do not fit within the image window, increase the height or width window size.
Ensure the resolution window size is consistent within and across experimental groups for comparison purposes.
Select an appropriate capture frame rate for mature cells.
Acquire a complete contraction-relaxation cycle wave.
Connect the camera to the computer via USB 3.0 interface.
Capture and store images first in RAM.
Manually save the captured images on the computer's hard drive.
Assemble the cell-stimulation chamber and fix it onto the stage of the microscope.
Set the temperature to 37°C.
Position the recording chamber and platinum electrodes for field stimulation.
Turn on the stimulator and set up parameters (frequency, voltage, pulse width duration).
Resuspend dissociated adult-CM in Tyrode solution.
Gently homogenize the cell solution.
Add a few drops of cells into the chamber at 37°C until the experiment starts.
Wait at least 1 minute for cells to settle.
Select a healthy cardiomyocyte and position it in the center of the field of view.
Rotate the camera as necessary to align the long axis of the cell with the horizontal axis of the image window.
Adjust the adult-CM image focus as described for different cell types.
Start the camera recorder.
Turn on the stimulator.
Choose the pacing condition based on the experiment goal.
Acquire cell contractility.
Make a preparation of neonatal-CM or hiPSC-CM that has several separated syncytium and spontaneously contracting cells.
Turn on the chamber at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Put the recipient containing the culture cells in the microscope chamber.
Wait at least 5 min to stabilize the cell temperature at 37°C.
Select the cell in the region of interest (ROI) in the camera image field according to the steps described.
Select a time interval in the wave detection window.
Display a zoomed plot of the selected interval below the top panel.
Simultaneously view cell image and derived contraction-relaxation wave.
Acquire speed of contraction at different points along the cycle.
Determine time intervals between important phases of contraction-relaxation cycle.
Measure shortening area in calibrated units.
